- deviation_metric: "Coefficient of variation (CV); Person-based similarity index (PBSI)"
- association_analysis: "Group comparisons of CV and PBSI scores. Spearman's rho test for associations between PBSI scores and clinical variables. Normative modeling to compare deviant and other patients."
- key_findings_brief: "The cerebral cortex in patients with schizophrenia showed greater structural variability than in healthy controls, and this was associated with lower general intelligence."
- key_findings_detailed: "Patients with schizophrenia had a higher coefficient of variation (CV) of surface area and cortical thickness in some regions. All person-based similarity index (PBSI) scores were lower in patients. PBSI scores for gray matter volume and all cortical measures positively correlated with full-scale IQ scores. Patients with deviant PBSI scores for gray matter volume and all cortical measures had lower full-scale IQ scores."
- key_limitations: "The cross-sectional design limits causal inferences. The study did not consider variations from race, education, or socioeconomic status in the harmonization process. Cumulative exposure to antipsychotics was not considered. The analysis of cognitive functions was limited due to a small number of tests."
- application_notes: "The findings provide neurobiological evidence for the heterogeneity of schizophrenia, particularly in relation to general intelligence. This may contribute to the development of individualized diagnosis and treatment plans for patients with schizophrenia."
